pages.title: Introduction to the module on Array Operations
pages.content:
All right - things are now getting serious! \
In this module on **Array Operations** - we will learn the concepts required to successfully perform beginner level array construction and manipulation required in programming problems.

Let's revise some basic syntax about arrays in the IDE that we came across in "Learn C++". 
- Arrays are used to store multiple items in a single variable
- Array items can be accessed by referring to their index.
  - $array[3]$ refers to the $4^{th}$ item of the array

Go to the IDE to revise the the above.

pages.title: Review problem - 1
pages.content:
Chef recorded a video explaining his favorite recipe. However, the size of the video is too large to upload on the internet. He wants to compress the video so that it has the minimum size possible. 

Chef's video has $N$ frames initially. The value of the $i^{th}$ frame is $A_i$. Chef can do the following type of operation **any** number of times:
- Choose an index $i$ $(1\le i \le N)$ such that the value of the $i^{th}$ frame is **equal** to the value of **either** of its neighbors and **remove** the $i^{th}$ frame. 

Find the **minimum** number of frames Chef can achieve.

pages.title: Predefined functions
pages.content:
## Predefined functions

C programs execute from `main`. This page introduces **User defined / Pre defined functions** and the syntax and runtime behaviour needed to use the concept correctly.

callout.title: Key Concept
callout.text: Focus on the C language rule illustrated by Predefined functions.

codeCard.code:
#include <stdio.h>
int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}int main(void){printf("%d\n",add(7,5));return 0;}

checkpoint.question: Which statement is correct about User defined / Pre defined functions in C?
options: It follows the C language rules and the specified input/output contract for User defined / Pre defined functions.
It can ignore declared data types and input format.
It should depend on undefined compiler behaviour.
It must use global variables for every value.
checkpoint.explanation: The first option correctly describes how User defined / Pre defined functions should be applied in C.

#include <stdio.h>
int main(void){int a[]={5,1,4,2,3},n=5;for(int i=0;i<n-1;i++)for(int j=0;j<n-1-i;j++)if(a[j]>a[j+1]){int x=a[j];a[j]=a[j+1];a[j+1]=x;}for(int i=0;i<n;i++)printf("%d ",a[i]);putchar('\n');return 0;}
